title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Lercanidipin, ATC C08CA13 für die Zeit 01.04.2026 - 31.03.2028 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate)
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Lercanidipin, ATC C08CA13, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.04.2026 in Kraft und endet am 31.03.2028 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate). Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – 81322998-Development of a project pipeline for the CAFI Cameroon Partnership and related activities
description: As part of its ongoing efforts to pursue its sustainable development goals and achieve the ambitions set out by the Government in its vision for 2035, Cameroon adopted in 2020, to implement the second phase of its vision covering the period 2020-2030, a policy document entitled the National Development Strategy 2020-2030 (SND30). During this phase, the Government intends to bring about the structural transformation of the economy through industrialisation. However, achieving these objectives will require well-structured measures designed to minimise the impact on the environment, particularly in light of the growing momentum of environmental protection initiatives promoted within the framework of the various Conferences of the Parties on climate change (COP), the most recent of which (COP 31) was held in Recife, Brazil, from 10. - 21. November 2025. With a view to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, Cameroon has joined the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI), which aims to recognise and preserve the value of the region"s forests in order to mitigate climate change and reduce poverty. More specifically, the long-term objective of the Cameroon-CAFI partnership is to facilitate the acceleration of economic development by promoting the application of the principle of a "green economy" through which Cameroonian value chains are made competitive and meet the demands of international, national and sub-regional markets, whilst Cameroon ensures food security and reduces the impact of the development of these sectors on deforestation and forest degradation. This is in line with the principles set out in the SND30 and defined in the Letter of Intent (LOI) signed between Cameroon and CAFI in October 2024 with a view to realising the ambitions outlined in the sectoral strategies and will underpin the success of the future partnership. In order to facilitate the consolidation and implementation of the Letter of Intent signed for a long-term partnership between Cameroon and CAFI, the partners have decided to envisage a three-year pilot phase. Furthermore, it was decided to implement a sectoral and multi-level coordination project, which will also oversee the portfolio management and coordination of three technical projects funded by CAFI. Its aim will be to strengthen the capacities of national technical bodies for enhanced and inclusive cross-sectoral coordination, and for strategic and spatial planning, in order to move towards a green economy. This coordination aims to build consensus on the planning tools to be developed, the reforms to be implemented and the innovative financing mechanisms for the development of the green economy, which will help to increase the mobilisation and alignment of interventions and funding from the public and private sectors, both national and international.

title: Servicii de monitorizare GPS a flotei CNPR si dispecerizare transport valori, prin acord cadru pe 3 ani
description:
Conditiile legale de securitate pentru transportul de valori impun monitorizarea GPS si dispecerizarea tuturor autovehiculelor care efectueaza acest tip de serviciu postal. Serviciile de dispecerizare si monitorizare a transportului de bunuri si valori monetare vor fi asigurate prin dispecerat autorizat de catre IGPR conform normelor legale in vigoare.(Legea 333/2003 si H.G. 301/2012, Cap.IV, art 55,56,61). Reglementarile legale nu permit transport de valori decat cu vehicule amenajate special, monitorizate GPS si dispecerizate prin dispecerat autorizat IGPR. Numarul de zile pana la care se pot solicita clarificari inainte de data limita de depunere a ofertelor este de 18 zile. Entitatea contractanta va raspunde in mod clar si complet tuturor solicitarilor de clarificari sau informatiilor suplimentare in a 11-a zi inainte de data limita de depunere a ofertelor. Entitatea contractantă va răspunde la solicitările de clarificări adresate de operatorii economici până la termenul-limită stabilit. (cu respectarea art.173, alin.2 din Legea nr.99/2016).

title: ADHA SECURITY MODULE - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.

description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Pridinol, ATC M03BX03, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.04.2026 in Kraft und endet am 31.03.2028 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate). Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (DPS) kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin osallistumispyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä "DPS hankinnan kuvaus ja ehdot”. Tilaaja määrittelee kussakin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä tarjouspyynnössä tarkemmin hankintajärjestelmässä kilpailutettavat kohteet sekä niiden vaatimukset. Hankintasopimukseen perustuvia hankintoja (tilauksia) voidaan tehdä hankintasopimuksen päättymiseen saakka. Hankintamenettely on kaksivaiheinen. Päästäkseen jättämään tarjouksia toimittajan on ensin jätettävä osallistumishakemus ja tultava hyväksytyksi hankintajärjestelmään. Tämän jälkeen toimittaja voi tehdä tarjouksia vastaamalla hankintayksikön lähettämään tarjouspyyntöön. Hankintayksikkö toteuttaa jatkossa sisäisiä kilpailutuksia noin vuoden välein. title: VERIFICATION OF SMALL SATELLITE FITNESS FOR PURPOSE IN NEW APPLICATION DOMAINS - EXPRO+
description: Private investment has stimulated the development of several new small satellite systems within Europe over the last five years. These exploit the reduced technical risk associated with technologies coming from previous ESA and Member State funded developments and benefiting from parallel technology improvements (eg miniaturization, materials etc) so that standard commercial practices can be followed.However, in many cases the privately financed and operated satellites include technical characteristics that create the potential for exploitation in other user domains where there is less acceptance of EO or where technical effort would be required to develop and verify the required information products and services. This may be due to the fact that the sensors are in some way unique or that the the overall system offers unique performance capabilities. Addressing this asymmetric risk structure is routinely practiced within ESA programmes however and given the connections ESA has with a wide range of stakeholders and the experience in supporting diverse EO applications development, ESA is well placed to fund the required developments up to the point where fitness for purpose is demonstrated for a well defined and clearly engaged stakeholder community which can then be the basis for private sector funded follow-on developments and customer engagement. This Invitation to Tender addresses this gap in order to generate an acceptable risk pattern for private sector investors (and the satellite operators) to support the necessary operationalization and commercialization activities. The overall objectives to be achieved are:(i) Accelerate the update of data, information and services from European small satellite operators among customer segments that cannot be effectively addressed by such private sector entities alone(ii) Verify, together with key organizations within the target customer segments, that data, information and services from the small satellite operators address an agreed set of priority issues/gaps and the demonstrated operational performance and processes are consistent with customer segment working practices and are therefore considered to be fit for purposeThis will require the contractor to engage a clear set of customers with requirements that cannot be presently addressed but which could be addressed by modifications to or with a small satellite system currently in operationIdentify a clear set of developments associated with the small satellite system in order to address the requirements of the stakeholders being targeted on a timeframe that is of immediate interest to the target stakeholdersElaborate verification exercises that enable a sufficiently convincing demonstration and verificationthat the developments executed have resulted in the enhanced small satellite system being capable to provide the required information under actual operational conditions to a performance level that is considered acceptable and within working practices that are compliant with the stakeholders operational environment. This should include a clear definition as to what are these threshold performance levels as well as a credible prospect of follow-on commercial uptake if these agreed performance levels are sufficiently well achievedIdentify follow-on mechanisms that can credibly support a transition to full commercial uptake
